You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: When must a GitLab employee have their laptop wiped?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): On your last day.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Offboarding FAQ > Timing > Your Laptop and Account steps > Laptop Wipe]
It is required that your laptop is wiped on your last day. Please [book an appointment](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/end-user-services/laptop-management/laptop-wipe//) with an IT Ops team member for your last day.

Under **no circumstance** should you be wiping your own laptop. Laptop wipes must be done from an IT Ops team member for logs. Please contact IT via the Compass app in Slack (type "Compass" in the top search bar to find it) or it-help@gitlab.com.

[GitLab Internal Acceptable Use Policy > Purpose > Procedure > Bring-Your-Own-Device (BYOD) > Unable to Use Company Laptop]
For new employees who have not received a company laptop, there are [exception processes](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/end-user-services/laptop-management/laptop-ordering/#exception-processes) for using non-company devices.

The same exception processes apply in the case of a corporate laptop being unavailable or unusable due to loss, theft or disrepair. See [lost or stolen procedures](/handbook/security#reporting-an-incident) for additional information. You must open [a Policy Exeption Request](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/gl-security/security-assurance/sec-compliance/exceptions/issues/new?issuable_template=exception_request). While the exception processes are considered a temporary solution, you still need to make sure the non-company system meets [basic configuration standards](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/end-user-services/laptop-management/laptop-security), and a Microsoft Windows system is still not allowed access under any circumstances.

Do not sign in to any GitLab related accounts using public computers, such as library or hotel kiosks.

[GitLab Offboarding > Offboarding Overview > Offboarding Support]
For system access questions and [laptop wipes](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/eta/corporate-it/end-user-services/gitlab-laptop-offboarding/) related to offboarding, send an email to `gitlab-laptop-recovery@gitlab.com`.

For payroll questions or outstanding expense claims, please reach out to either `uspayroll@gitlab.com` or `nonuspayroll@gitlab.com`.

For any other offboarding questions from active team members please reach out to People Operations via [Compass](https://app.serval.com/new-request) or send an email to `people_operations@gitlab.com` if your access has already been terminated.

**Note:** If a termination date changes, please reach out to People Operations via Compass. The team will update Workday.  The notice is used as supporting documentation of the change and is saved in the team members Workday record.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
A GitLab employee must have their laptop wiped on their last day [1].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
